summary: Tested HEMELEY CamPay (Cameroon Mobile Money) integration via pure httpx (NO pip SDK). 11/12 backend tests pass; 1 skip is due to seed data (no menu portions available), not a CamPay defect. All Pydantic validations (amount >= 25, phone format), phone normalization (+237/0/9-digit local), happy-path POST /api/campay/collect, MongoDB persistence in campay_transactions, GET /api/campay/status/{ref} normalization, and 502 error on invalid reference are verified.

minor.issue: CamPay sandbox enforces per-phone rate limit (~1 req/min). When hit, backend correctly surfaces it as 502 ('CAMPAY error 429: Rate limit per Phone number exceeded'). Tests now use unique phones to avoid this.

Seeded menu (poulet DG) has remaining_portions=0 → checkout returns 400 'Not enough portions'. Integration with CamPay collect (lines 298-328 in routes_order.py) could not be E2E-tested. Code review of routes_order.py confirms campay_client.initiate_payment + persistence of campay_reference/campay_status='PENDING' is wired correctly.

action_items: (Optional) Re-seed at least one menu with remaining_portions > 0 to enable E2E checkout→CamPay integration testing in the future.
(Optional) Consider adding a small retry/backoff or surface a more user-friendly message when CamPay returns 429 for the same phone within 60s (currently surfaced as raw 502).

No code changes required for the CamPay endpoints — implementation conforms to the 10-step CamPay guide: permanent token + dynamic fallback, exact 'Authorization: Token {token}' header, /token/, /collect/, /transaction/{ref}/ endpoints, lazy env props resolve the load_dotenv timing bug.
critical_code_review_comments: campay.py: lazy @property pattern for env vars correctly resolves the load_dotenv-at-import-time race condition. Good.
campay.py: _request_with_retry refreshes token only on 401/403 (correct). Other 4xx are surfaced as 502 with truncated body — clean.

routes_payment.py: campay_router endpoints are public-by-design (no auth dependency) — confirm this is intended (it matches the spec but exposes a payment-initiation surface; consider rate-limiting per IP/phone at the FastAPI layer if abuse becomes a concern).
routes_payment.py: campay_transactions insert wrapped in try/except — failures are only logged. Acceptable for audit table but means a DB outage will not block the user-facing /collect response.

routes_order.py L298-328: payment_method 'orange'/'mtn' triggers CamPay collect AFTER the order is inserted; failures only mark campay_status='FAILED' — the order itself is not rolled back. Verify this is the intended UX (probably yes, customer can retry from the order detail screen).

success_rate.backend: 92% (11/12 pass, 1 skip due to seed data, 0 fail)

test_credentials: Public endpoints — no auth required for /api/campay/* by design
seed_data_creation: None. Tests create transient campay_transactions rows tied to throw-away phone numbers (237 + random 9 digits). campay_transactions docs are left in DB for audit; they have TEST_REF_ or HEMELEY- external_reference prefixes for easy cleanup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: CamPay integration is solid. test_campay.py covers: 4 validation tests (422/400), 5 happy-path tests (UUID reference, ussd_code, operator, status, MongoDB persistence, phone normalization +237/0X/9-digit/custom external_reference), 2 status endpoint tests, 1 order-checkout integration (skipped due to seed). If you need to re-run, wait 60s between consecutive calls using the same phone OR rely on the unique-phone fixture already in tests. Demo CamPay caps amount at 25 XAF; any test using amount > 25 will fail at the CamPay side, not the backend.
